From e272f7ec070d212b9301d5a465bc8952f8dcf908 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Nov 2019 20:02:51 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] gpio: lynxpoint: Setup correct IRQ handlers

When commit 75e99bf5ed8f ("gpio: lynxpoint: set default handler to be
handle_bad_irq()") switched default handler to be handle_bad_irq() the
lp_irq_type() function remained untouched. It means that even request_irq()
can't change the handler and we are not able to handle IRQs properly anymore.
Fix it by setting correct handlers in the lp_irq_type() callback.

Fixes: 75e99bf5ed8f ("gpio: lynxpoint: set default handler to be handle_bad_irq()")
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20191118180251.31439-1-andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>

diff --git a/drivers/gpio/gpio-lynxpoint.c b/drivers/gpio/gpio-lynxpoint.c
index e9e47c0d5be7..490ce7bae25e 100644
--- a/drivers/gpio/gpio-lynxpoint.c
+++ b/drivers/gpio/gpio-lynxpoint.c
@@ -164,6 +164,12 @@ static int lp_irq_type(struct irq_data *d, unsigned type)
 		value |= TRIG_SEL_BIT | INT_INV_BIT;
 
 	outl(value, reg);
+
+	if (type & IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH)
+		irq_set_handler_locked(d, handle_edge_irq);
+	else if (type & IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_MASK)
+		irq_set_handler_locked(d, handle_level_irq);
+
 	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&lg->lock, flags);
 
 	return 0;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/gpio/gpio-lynxpoint.c`**
- The `lp_irq_type()` function was modified to set the correct IRQ handlers based on the type of interrupt.
- Specifically, if the interrupt type is `IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH`, it sets the handler to `handle_edge_irq`. If the type is a level-triggered interrupt (indicated by `IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_MASK`), it sets the handler to `handle_level_irq`.
- This change ensures that the IRQ handlers can be properly set and that interrupts can be handled correctly, addressing the issue introduced by a previous commit.

### Relationships
- The modifications in `gpio-lynxpoint.c` directly address a bug introduced by commit `75e99bf5ed8f`, which changed the default IRQ handler to `handle_bad_irq()`. The previous implementation did not allow for the proper setting of IRQ handlers, leading to improper handling of interrupts.
- By updating the `lp_irq_type()` function to set the correct handlers, this patch fixes the functionality that was broken by the earlier commit, thereby restoring the ability to handle IRQs appropriately.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
// Default handler set to handle_bad_irq()
lp_irq_type() function did not set correct IRQ handlers
request_irq() can't change the handler
```
Reason:
The `lp_irq_type()` function was not updated to set the correct IRQ handlers after the default handler was changed to `handle_bad_irq()`. This oversight meant that even when `request_irq()` was called, the handler could not be modified, leading to improper handling of interrupts.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (type & IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH)
    irq_set_handler_locked(d, handle_edge_irq);
else if (type & IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_MASK)
    irq_set_handler_locked(d, handle_level_irq);
```
Reason:
These statements in the `lp_irq_type()` function set the appropriate IRQ handlers based on the type of interrupt (edge or level). This ensures that the correct handler is assigned, allowing for proper handling of interrupts when `request_irq()` is called.
